title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1LC1LF_1RA0LD_1LB1LA_1RB1RC_---0LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1LC1LF_1RA0LD_1LB1LA_1RB1RC_---0LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of blocks of the word 110. Its main move is an exact transfer cycle between three neighbouring blocks: (x, y, z) → (x−2, y+3, z−1) in 28y+111 steps, checked on all 8,397 cycles in the first 108 steps. Lean proves the shift rules inside blocks. What happens when a cycle runs out, and so the map on whole lists, is not known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 34,337 cells have been visited and 22,887 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: a_right: going right, A shifts a block of n words 110 by one cell (3n+1 steps). d_left and c_left: going left, D and C cross a block written as 110 or 101 words. All three hold for every n and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: The transfer cycle
claims.text: When the tape around the head reads (110)^x 0 (110)^y 1 A> 1 0 1 0 1 1 0 0 (110)^z 0, the next turn in state A at the same place finds (x, y, z) changed to (x−2, y+3, z−1) after exactly 28y+111 steps. All 8,397 such cycles in the first 108 steps follow this, step count included.

claims.title: Why it is hard
claims.text: The main move is a 3-for-2 exchange between three neighbouring blocks, the arithmetic of Collatz-like machines. Each cycle is exact, but which blocks meet next depends on how earlier cycles ended, and those end rules are not known yet.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts if F reads a 0.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The machine sweeps over a row of blocks. Crossing a block is a plain shift, but at each boundary something more complicated happens: the one-cell separator flips between 0 and 1, and the neighbouring blocks trade length in a way that is not understood yet.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 34,337 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Blocks of 110 and one-cell separators
html: At the right end the tape is 10 (110)^x0 0 (110)^x1 0 ... 0 (110)^3 1. At the left end the same blocks are separated by a mix of 0s and 1s. Crossing the inside of a block is a plain shift by one cell (three Lean rules). The changes happen at the separators.
Many sweeps turn back before they reach an end, so these rows are far apart. The rule that takes one row to the next is the open part.

sections.heading: A 3-for-2 transfer
html: Most of the work is one local cycle. When the head turns in state A at (110)^x 0 (110)^y 1 A> 1 0 1 0 1 1 0 0 (110)^z 0, it zigzags left and right and comes back to the same place with the left block two words shorter, the right block one word shorter, and the middle block three words longer:
(x, y, z) → (x−2, y+3, z−1) in exactly 28y+111 steps.

All 8,397 cycles in the first 108 steps obey this, step count included. Paying two to get three is the arithmetic of Collatz-like machines, and it is why the block lengths look irregular. The rules for what happens when a cycle runs out (x below 2, or z at 0) are the next thing to find.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.545). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 34,337 cells (21,079 left of the start, 763 right), with a density of 1s of 0.667.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A list of 110-blocks whose main move is an exact transfer cycle (x, y, z) -> (x-2, y+3, z-1) in 28y+111 steps between three neighbouring blocks, a 3-for-2 exchange; the rules at the end of a cycle are not known.
family: block list with a 3-for-2 transfer cycle (Collatz-like)
